summary_html: Federal **OIG** investigations and **Single Audit Act** reviews track misuse of child-welfare funds. Project Milk Carton aggregates audit findings and highlights unresolved repeat deficiencies.
authority_html:
- **Inspector General Act (5 U.S.C. App.)** — OIG oversight of HHS  
- **Single Audit Act (31 U.S.C. §§ 7501–7507)** — audits of federally funded programs

primary_citations.citation_text: District of Columbia - D.C. Code Title 4, Chapter 13 (Child Abuse and Neglect)

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: United States District Court for the District of Columbia
key_cases.holding: After trial the court found the District's child welfare system violated federal and District statutory and constitutional requirements at nearly every stage, including a consistent failure to provide services or make reasonable efforts to prevent placement, and ordered systemic relief.
key_cases.relevance: Its findings on service capacity and record-keeping are the template for auditing where District child welfare money does and does not go.
key_cases.quote: the Court finds that defendants have consistently failed to provide services or otherwise use “reasonable efforts” to prevent placement

key_cases.case_name: Vining v. Council of the District of Columbia
key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: The Council may not invoke the Legislative Privilege Act through D.C. FOIA Exemption 6 (or, on this record, Exemption 4) to withhold documents responsive to a FOIA request, and summary judgment for the Council was reversed.
key_cases.relevance: It preserves public access to the Council records that document agency spending and performance.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that the Legislative Privilege Act cannot be invoked through Exemption 6 so as to permit the Council to withhold documents responsive to a FOIA request

key_cases.case_name: District of Columbia v. Fraternal Order of Police, Metropolitan Police Department Labor Committee
key_cases.court: District of Columbia Court of Appeals
key_cases.holding: Under D.C. FOIA's personal privacy exemption the negligible public interest in the identities of employees who sent emails under a pledge of confidentiality did not outweigh their privacy interest, so the District was entitled to withhold the identifying information.
key_cases.relevance: It governs redaction of individual identities in audit-related District records released under FOIA.
key_cases.quote: we conclude that FOIA does not require the District of Columbia to disclose the identities of the email authors

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately if MPD deems the child critical missing; otherwise once the child has been missing more than 30 days (MPD makes the NCMEC report)
timeline_requirements.starts_from: CFSA files a missing person report with MPD immediately after discovering the child is missing (D.C. Code § 4-1323.01(a))
